elements.content: Communication Goal: I can ask and answer names and introduce another person.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 1. FIRST CONTACT & PERSONAL IDENTITY
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: My Name Is... Asking Names
- Materials: Vocabulary cards, audio for the listening, reading handout, COSYmanuals A1 grammar pages for questions with 'be', short answers.
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles greetings and the verb be from Lesson 1.1.
Recycled language from the previous lesson: name, first name.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (5 items):

name — the word people use for a person. Example: My name is Marta.
first name — the name your family gives you. Example: Her first name is Lucia.
surname — your family name. Example: My surname is Rossi.
who — a question word for people. Example: Who is that man?
what — a question word for things. Example: What is your name?
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What is your name?
• My name is...
• Who is he?
• This is my friend.
• How do you spell it?
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the word people use for a person'?
Which word means 'the name your family gives you'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Yes/no questions rise at the end.
Are you a student? ↗
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word has the target sound?
Mark the stressed syllable.
Grammar focus: Questions with 'be', short answers.
For questions, put the verb be first: Are you a student? Is he your teacher? Answer with a short answer: Yes, I am. No, I'm not. Yes, she is.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
___ you a student?
Is he your teacher? Choose the correct answer.
Complete the sentence.
Reading (Short dialogues at a conference):
A: Hello, what is your name? B: My name is Daniel. A: And who is this? B: This is Lucia, my friend.
What is the man's name?
Listening (People asking and giving names):
A: What is your name? B: My name is Peter. A: Who is she? B: She is Maria, my friend.
What is his name?
Speaking: Asking names and introducing a friend in trios

• What is your name?
• My name is...
• Who is he?
Writing: Write short Q&A pairs introducing friends
